intro: Castellammare di Stabia has two old trees in a royal garden and a third that nobody can agree on. Up the hill, in the garden of the Reggia di Quisisana, the Campania region dates a great pine and a twisted yew to 1765, in the reign of Ferdinand IV, and both still stand by the King's first fountain. Down on the seafront, the Villa Comunale holds a towering araucaria that the national register calls a monkey puzzle and a 2022 photograph shows as a Norfolk Island pine.
meta_description: Old trees of Castellammare di Stabia: a pine and a yew dated to 1765 in the Quisisana royal garden, and a disputed araucaria on the seafront.
question_meta: What is the oldest tree in Castellammare di Stabia? A pine and a yew in the Quisisana garden, dated by the region to 1765.
question_answer: The oldest trees in Castellammare di Stabia are a pine and a yew in the garden of the Reggia di Quisisana. The Campania region says both have stood there since 1765, making them roughly two and a half centuries old. The pine is the bigger, 495 centimetres round and 22 metres tall.
question_context: The two oldest trees stand together by the King's first fountain in the historic garden of the Reggia di Quisisana, on the hill above the town. The Campania region dates both to 1765, in the reign of Ferdinand IV, king of Naples, and its dating is the only one there is. The pine is the largest of the garden, 495 centimetres round and 22 metres tall, though the region calls it an Aleppo pine while the national register lists the Calabrian variety. The yew is only 8 metres tall, with a twisted trunk and crown. Since 2020 the garden has belonged to the Parco archeologico di Pompei, and it is visited with the archaeological museum of Stabia in the palace, on a ticket. The third tree is free to see, in the Villa Comunale on the seafront, ten minutes from the station. Its species is disputed. The register says monkey puzzle, 30 metres tall, while a 2022 photograph shows the level, drooping tiers of a Norfolk Island pine of about 20 metres.

faq.q: Is the Quisisana garden open to visitors?
faq.a: Yes, on a ticket, as part of the Parco archeologico di Pompei together with the Stabia archaeological museum. Listings disagree on opening days and price, so check pompeiisites.org first.

faq.q: Is the araucaria in the Villa Comunale a monkey puzzle?
faq.a: Italy's national register says so, but a 2022 photograph shows a Norfolk Island pine, which fits its size better. We give both names. If you can settle it, tell us.

faq.q: How do I get to the trees?
faq.a: The Circumvesuviana stops at Castellammare di Stabia. The Villa Comunale is about 10 minutes on foot; Quisisana is a steep walk or a local bus up the hill.

trees.name: The Aleppo Pine of Quisisana

location.address: Reggia di Quisisana, Via Quisisana, 80053 Castellammare di Stabia

location_site.name: Historic garden of the Reggia di Quisisana

trees.story:
According to the Campania region, this pine has stood in the garden of the Reggia di Quisisana since 1765, in the reign of Ferdinand IV, king of Naples. That makes it roughly two and a half centuries old, and the region's dating is the only one we have.

It has grown into the largest pine of the garden, 495 centimetres round and 22 metres tall, figures the regional and national registers agree on. They do not agree on what it is. The region calls it an Aleppo pine. Italy's national register lists it as the Calabrian variety, Pinus halepensis var. brutia. The two are close relatives and hard to tell apart from the path, so we use the region's name and keep the question open. If you know your pines, tell us which it is.

Quisisana sits on the hill above Castellammare di Stabia, and the royal garden around it passed to the Parco archeologico di Pompei in 2020. The palace now holds the archaeological museum of Stabia, so the pine shares its ticket with the finds of a Roman town.

We have found no recent dated photograph of the tree. Opening days and ticket prices vary between listings, so check the Pompeii sites page before you climb the hill.

official_register.name: Elenco degli alberi monumentali d'Italia (MASAF), sheet 02/C129/NA/15

trees.access: Ticketed. The historic garden of the Reggia di Quisisana has been part of the Parco archeologico di Pompei since 2020 and is visited with the Museo Archeologico di Stabia; listings disagree on opening days and ticket price, so check pompeiisites.org before going.
trees.transport: Circumvesuviana train to Castellammare di Stabia, then a steep walk or a local bus up the hill to Quisisana.
trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it as the biggest pine in the garden, a trunk nearly 5 metres round and 22 metres tall, standing by the King's first fountain near a low, twisted yew.
trees.verify_notes: MASAF 495 cm, 22 m, species 'Pinus halepensis var. brutia' (Calabrian Pine); Campania regional scheda 62 (coord 40.684167,14.488889) gives Pinus halepensis, 495 cm, 22 m and says it has stood in the historic garden of the Palazzo Reale since 1765 under Ferdinand IV. Species conflict noted: Aleppo vs Calabrian pine, both close relatives; treated as Aleppo Pine per the regional scheda, flag it. 1765 is the source's date for the tree standing there, so age is 'about 260 years' at most, not a planting certificate: age left as a broad source-based range. No dated sighting. Recognise: the largest pine of the garden, beside the first King's fountain area.

trees.name: The Yew of Quisisana

location.address: Reggia di Quisisana, Via Quisisana, 80053 Castellammare di Stabia

location_site.name: Historic garden of the Reggia di Quisisana

trees.story:
The yew by the King's first fountain is only eight metres tall, and it has had about two and a half centuries to get there. The Campania region says it has stood in the historic garden of the Reggia di Quisisana since 1765.

Yews are slow, and this one shows its years in its shape rather than its height. The regional register describes a characteristic twisted trunk and a twisted crown, and both registers, regional and national, give the same measurements, 211 centimetres round and 8 metres high. It is a squat, contorted tree beside a fountain built for a king.

That king was Ferdinand IV of Naples, in whose reign the region dates this tree. The royal palace stands on the hill above Castellammare di Stabia, and since 2020 the garden has belonged to the Parco archeologico di Pompei, with the Stabia archaeological museum inside the palace. A much larger pine, which the region dates to the same year, stands close by, and between them they are the two old trees of the King's fountain.

We have no recent dated photograph of the yew. If you visit, tell us how it looks. Opening days and the ticket differ between listings, so check the Pompeii sites page first.

trees.verify_notes: MASAF 211 cm, 8 m; regional scheda 63 (coord 40.684167,14.489167) agrees (211 cm, 8 m) and says the tree has a characteristic twisted trunk and crown and stands near the first fountain of the King in the historic garden since 1765. No dated sighting. Recognise: a low twisted yew beside the first King's fountain.

trees.name: The Araucaria of the Villa Comunale

location.address: Villa Comunale, Viale Regina Elena, 80053 Castellammare di Stabia

trees.story:
Italy's national register says this is a monkey puzzle, 30 metres tall. A visitor's photograph from 2022 shows a Norfolk Island pine of about 20 metres, and the photograph has the stronger case.

Both trees are araucarias, the southern-hemisphere conifers that Mediterranean seafronts have planted for generations. They look nothing alike up close. A monkey puzzle carries stiff, sharp scale leaves on bare, rope-like branches. A Norfolk Island pine grows in neat level tiers of soft, drooping branches, like a stack of green shelves, and the 2022 picture shows exactly that, a tall whorled conifer rising above the apartment blocks. A monkey puzzle reaching 30 metres on a trunk 220 centimetres round would be unusual. A Norfolk Island pine of that size is ordinary.

So we call it an araucaria and give you both names. The register's girth of 220 centimetres stands either way, and so does the fact that it was alive and towering over the Villa Comunale, the public garden on Castellammare di Stabia's seafront, in February 2022.

Nobody has published when it was planted. If you know, or if you stand under it and can settle which araucaria it is, tell us.

The garden is free and open air, about ten minutes on foot from the station.

official_register.name: Elenco degli alberi monumentali d'Italia (MASAF), sheet 05/C129/NA/15

trees.access: Free. Public seafront garden (Villa Comunale), open air.
trees.transport: About 10 minutes' walk from Castellammare di Stabia station on the Circumvesuviana.
trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it as the tall conifer with branches in level, drooping tiers, rising above the apartment blocks on the seafront side of the Villa Comunale.
trees.verify_notes: MASAF lists Araucaria araucana (Monkey Puzzle), 220 cm, 30 m. Species conflict: an iNaturalist observation dated 2022-02-11 in the 'Giardini Pubblici', GPS 40.695554,14.480412 (about 9 m from the register point), is identified as Araucaria heterophylla (Norfolk Island Pine), cultivated, with the note 'H:20m'; the photo (viewed, not open licence) shows a tall conifer with whorled drooping branches above apartment blocks. A 30 m Monkey Puzzle at 220 cm girth is implausible while Norfolk Island Pine at that size is normal, so species is given generically and the page should ask readers. Alive 2022. Recognise: the tall whorled conifer in the garden near the apartment blocks on the seafront side.
